newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Floods submerge over 10,000 hectares in Romania.
newsitem.headline: Floods submerge over 10,000 hectares in Romania.

text.p: Romanian officials were keeping a keen eye on the rising water level of the River Danube on Friday after the week's heavy rains left more than 10,000 hectares (25,000 acres) under water.
The Environment Ministry said the floods, in which four people have died, had submerged 10,057 hectares, three times more than previous estimates.
Officials put losses in the worst hit region, Caras Severin in the west of the country, at $15.5 million, but the overall national cost of flood damage was not given.
Some 500 households had been damaged, they said.
The Agriculture Ministry gave no official crop-by-crop damage breakdown but said a forecast bumper wheat crop had been delayed by the rains.
It did not issue figures for wheat crop damage but the traditional granaries in southern and central Romania were not among the affected areas.
The International Grains Council (IGC) on Thursday cut its estimate for the Romanian wheat crop to 7.1 million tonnes in its latest Grains Market Report compared to previous 7.8 million forecast.
It would still be a huge improvement on last year's poor 3.2 million tonne harvest, the IGC said.
Local weather forecasters said they expected hot and sunny weather across most of the country, but predicted rainstorms and hail in western Romania, central Transylvania, and Oltenia in the south.
Flood monitors from the Environment Ministry said the level of the Danube was rising across the entire Romanian section from the southern border with Yugoslavia and Bulgaria to the Black Sea.
The levels of several smaller rivers were also rising, including the Prut, a tributary of the Danube, which forms the eastern border with the former Soviet republic of Moldova.
